options_ranked.title: Renewal-Indexed Pricing with Gated Premium Selling
options_ranked.description: Prepare and execute cost-indexed pricing at the next contractually permitted renewal, supported by revised sales incentives and customer-specific volume commitments. Target Synthetic Blend Engine Oil and Conventional Engine Oil, currently at 20.64% and 19.16% margin. Preserve existing list prices and contractual discounts during anchor-account locks. Retain the proposed High Mileage and Full Synthetic selling pathway only as a gated expansion: their actual margins are absent, so authorize no volume transfer until executable offers establish superior contribution after discounts and cost-to-serve. Exclude premium-transfer benefits from the quantified Synthetic Blend recovery. No named healthy product is available for replication; leave the periods identified in what_is_not as within threshold outside any blanket corrective program.
options_ranked.rationale: Price-volume-mix decomposition separates a directly actionable renewal-price mechanism from an unsupported premium-margin premise. The client-confirmed net_revenue relationship supports the margin mechanism, but neither customer acceptance nor the required renewal coverage is established.
options_ranked.time_to_value: Contract preparation and eligible selling changes in 0–90 days; material recovery at permitted renewals, potentially 3–12 months.

arguments_for: Renewal indexation addresses pricing rigidity without breaching the explicit mid-quarter list-price lock.
Customer profitability analysis supports differentiating offers by realized contribution rather than applying an indiscriminate increase.
arguments_against: High Mileage and Full Synthetic margins are not supplied, and the premium-mix relationship is explicitly an unconfirmed industry prior.
Renewal coverage and customer acceptance could limit realized recovery despite the 7.14-point Synthetic Blend gap.
key_questions: Which permitted renewals can carry the required effective price realization without reducing total gross profit?

arguments_for: An index tied to the purchased input specification can reduce future mismatch between customer terms and supplier costs, consistent with the listed COGS accounting relationships.
arguments_against: The input contains no quantified base-oil inflation, so an index alone may fail to address discount leakage, manufacturing costs or overhead absorption.
key_questions: Will the approved index, reset frequency and contractual lag track the costs actually incurred on the renewed products?

arguments_for: The premium-transfer gate avoids assuming that product positioning establishes attractive participation economics.
arguments_against: Renewing all existing volume could preserve structurally unattractive business; the Value category is already down 6.42 points.
key_questions: Which renewal offers should be declined when their post-renewal contribution remains below the approved participation floor?

implementation_triggers: A contract reaches its legally permitted renewal or reset date.
An executable renewal offer meets the approved retained-volume and gross-profit floors.
Premium selling incentives activate only when the proposed destination has demonstrably better realized contribution than the source product.
prerequisites: Legal approval of renewal dates, index provisions and all changes to customer economics.
Sales authority to negotiate differentiated offers and reject uneconomic commitments.
A compensation design that rewards realized gross profit rather than premium-product volume alone.

impact_estimate.basis: The retained Stage 1 range targets 2.8–4.2 percentage points of Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's 7.14-point decline through realized renewal pricing, implying 23.44–24.84% segment margin, conditional on approximately 3.66–5.59% effective segment-wide net-price improvement at unchanged unit COGS and volume.

key_assumptions.assumption: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil has a 7.14-point recovery gap relative to the prior period.
key_assumptions.provenance: The named change point reports 20.64% versus 27.78%.

key_assumptions.assumption: Permitted renewals provide sufficient coverage to realize an effective 3.66–5.59% segment-wide net-price increase.
key_assumptions.provenance: Signed renewal coverage multiplied by realized price uplift reaches the required effective segment-wide improvement.

key_assumptions.assumption: Customer retention and unit COGS remain sufficiently stable for the illustrated price-to-margin conversion.
key_assumptions.provenance: Renewed-account volume, unit COGS and gross-profit dollars remain within the approved offer guardrails.

key_assumptions.assumption: A subset of High Mileage or Full Synthetic offers has better contribution than the source business.
key_assumptions.provenance: Approved destination offers exceed source-product realized margin and contribution after incentives, freight and cannibalization.

flagged_side_effects: Customer attrition or lower volume can offset price realization.
Index mismatch can over-recover or under-recover actual input movements.
Premium incentives can cannibalize profitable sales; their benefit is excluded from this segment recovery estimate.

options_ranked.title: Supplier Cost Reset with Selective Forward Coverage
options_ranked.description: Replace the proposed procurement audit as the primary intervention with competitive supplier renegotiation, qualified-source substitution and selective fixed-price purchasing for affected formulations. Prioritize Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, then Conventional Engine Oil and Compressor Oil. Execute forward coverage only where delivered economics improve on the relevant purchasing baseline; locking today's price is protection against future increases, not recovery of an existing loss. Exclude customer repricing from this option. No healthy product benchmark is named, and the within-threshold periods in what_is_not do not justify an enterprise-wide procurement redesign.
options_ranked.rationale: Cost-to-serve and procurement mechanisms act through base-oil cost into COGS without changing locked customer prices. Parallel product deterioration is consistent with a common input pressure, but does not establish its existence or magnitude; procurement savings must come from lower delivered costs, not simply greater cost certainty.
options_ranked.time_to_value: Supplier concessions and qualified purchases in 0–90 days; recognized margin benefit as lower-cost inventory is consumed, potentially 3–6 months.

arguments_for: Supplier savings can improve economics during the contractual price-lock period without asking anchor customers for a prohibited increase.
arguments_against: The option leaves customer discounting and renewal architecture unchanged even though the confirmed net_revenue relationship also permits a revenue-side explanation.
key_questions: Can sourcing changes preserve customer-approved specifications and service commitments without concessions that consume savings?

arguments_for: Qualified supplier competition directly targets an account that the client confirms contributes to COGS.
Separating price protection from realized savings prevents treating a fixed-price contract as automatic margin recovery.
arguments_against: Stage 1 attributes only 60–75% of the 7.14-point loss to base oil, equivalent to 4.28–5.36 points, below the 6.8-point upper anchor.
Inventory accounting and consumption lags can postpone reported recovery after procurement execution.
key_questions: Do signed delivered-cost terms yield the required total COGS reduction after qualification costs, freight, working capital and inventory timing?

arguments_for: A time-bounded supplier reset preserves participation choices while avoiding premature withdrawal from products that may remain economically viable.
arguments_against: Long forward commitments can lock the business into formulations whose economics later warrant de-emphasis.
key_questions: Can coverage volumes be capped at committed demand to avoid obstructing later assortment changes?

implementation_triggers: A qualified supplier submits enforceable delivered-cost terms that improve expected realized economics.
Quality and operations approve the substitute source before production use.
Forward coverage remains within authorized committed demand and treasury exposure limits.
prerequisites: Supplier-switch authority and approved formulation specifications.
Treasury approval of fixed-price exposure, collateral requirements and counterparty limits.
Purchase-order amendments that preserve service levels and avoid excess inventory commitments.

impact_estimate.basis: The retained Stage 1 range represents 4.2–6.8 percentage points of Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's 7.14-point decline and requires approximately 5.29–8.57% lower total segment COGS at unchanged revenue, a conditional supplier-reset target rather than a benefit established by forward coverage.

key_assumptions.assumption: Reducing base-oil cost can reduce COGS and improve Gross Margin % at unchanged revenue.
key_assumptions.provenance: Client-confirmed base_oil_cost-to-cogs component relationship and direct cogs-to-gross_margin_pct accounting relationship.

key_assumptions.assumption: Addressable base-oil purchasing costs explain a material share of the observed deterioration.
key_assumptions.provenance: Realized savings on executed base-oil purchases materially lower affected-product unit COGS relative to the current purchasing baseline.

key_assumptions.assumption: Suppliers can deliver enough savings to reduce total Synthetic Blend COGS by approximately 5.29–8.57%.
key_assumptions.provenance: Executed supplier terms and consumed inventory produce the required reduction after all switching and financing costs.

key_assumptions.assumption: Qualified substitutes preserve formulation performance and customer service.
key_assumptions.provenance: Released production batches meet specifications without higher rejection rates, expedited freight or customer claims.

flagged_side_effects: Fixed-price commitments can become unfavorable if spot prices fall.
Supplier concentration or substitution can introduce quality and continuity risks.
Hedge accounting and inventory consumption can separate cash savings from reported Gross Margin %.

options_ranked.title: Selective Assortment Withdrawal and Capacity Consolidation
options_ranked.description: Turn the proposed cost waterfall and reallocation decision into staged withdrawal of contractually discretionary, low-contribution SKU-channel combinations and consolidation of retained production runs. Target the affected Synthetic Blend and Conventional portfolios; treat Value as a separate reported category rather than asserting unprovided product membership. Quantify recovery only within retained Synthetic Blend business. Do not redirect volume automatically to Compressor Oil: its 28% margin is higher than Synthetic Blend's 20.64%, but it also declined 5.86 points and serves different applications; first restore its account economics and establish demand substitutability before any reallocation. No named healthy benchmark supports replication, and the within-threshold periods require no blanket intervention.
options_ranked.rationale: Portfolio participation analysis challenges whether every existing order deserves retention, while overhead absorption diagnostics guard against mistaking allocated costs for avoidable savings. Product deterioration supports targeting these portfolios, but does not establish structural category decline or identify specific exit candidates.
options_ranked.time_to_value: Contract-compliant assortment changes in 3–6 months; capacity consolidation and durable benefits in 6–12 months or longer.

arguments_for: Customer profitability analysis supports declining low-contribution discretionary offers rather than using prohibited mid-quarter list-price increases.
arguments_against: Product exit can damage an anchor-account bundle or reduce profitable adjacent purchases; the supplied product deltas do not establish customer-level exit economics.
key_questions: Which proposed withdrawals preserve contractual fulfillment and positive account-level gross profit after lost adjacent sales?

arguments_for: Consolidated runs can act through manufacturing and packaging costs, both listed components of COGS.
arguments_against: Reduced volume can worsen fixed-cost absorption, so removing an apparently low-margin SKU does not automatically remove its allocated overhead.
key_questions: Which shifts, purchase commitments or physical resources will actually be removed when a SKU-channel combination is withdrawn?

arguments_for: Staged withdrawal creates a participation choice rather than assuming prior-year margin is the correct target for every product.
arguments_against: No market signal establishes structural decline, and Compressor Oil's own 5.86-point deterioration prevents treating it as an uncomplicated growth destination.
key_questions: Does each withdrawal improve cash contribution after stranded costs, transition expense and account-bundle effects?

implementation_triggers: A discretionary SKU-channel combination fails the approved contribution floor after feasible commercial and operating terms.
Legal confirms that withdrawal does not breach supply commitments or alter locked prices.
Operations commits to specific avoidable resource reductions before an exit is authorized.
prerequisites: Approved participation floors and gross-profit-dollar safeguards.
Customer transition provisions, inventory run-down plans and contractual release where needed.
An executable capacity-removal plan rather than a reallocation of overhead charges.

impact_estimate.basis: The retained Stage 1 range targets 2.5–4.5 percentage points of Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's 7.14-point decline through lower-cost retained production and selective withdrawal, implying 23.14–25.14% margin on the retained segment but not necessarily higher gross-profit dollars.

key_assumptions.assumption: The product portfolios selected for intervention have materially deteriorated.
key_assumptions.provenance: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil declined 7.14 points and Conventional Engine Oil declined 6.61 points.

key_assumptions.assumption: Some SKU-channel combinations have sufficiently weak contribution to justify withdrawal.
key_assumptions.provenance: Approved withdrawal cases show improved retained-business cash contribution after lost sales and transition costs.

key_assumptions.assumption: Capacity consolidation removes actual costs rather than shifting allocations.
key_assumptions.provenance: Payroll, supplier commitments or other manufacturing and packaging expenditures fall following the specified resource removals.

key_assumptions.assumption: Customer spillovers and stranded costs do not outweigh the retained-segment margin gain.
key_assumptions.provenance: Total account contribution and enterprise gross-profit dollars remain above the approved post-withdrawal floors.

flagged_side_effects: Gross Margin % can increase while revenue and gross-profit dollars decline.
Lower throughput can worsen overhead absorption.
Withdrawal can sacrifice customer relationships, shelf space and future restart flexibility.

solutions.recommendation_rationale: As the requested first-move sequencing choice, renewal-indexed pricing addresses Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's decline from 27.78% to 20.64% through the client-confirmed net-revenue mechanism while preserving the anchor-account mid-quarter list-price lock. Authorization should cover permitted renewal execution, not a guaranteed recovery commitment or an ungated premium shift; the alternatives remain independent choices, not a council consensus.

problem_reframe.situation: Gross Margin % declined overall. The problem statement reports a 7.14-percentage-point drop to 20.64%, but those values match Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, not the enterprise aggregate. The aggregate analysis reports 29.94% versus 34.43%, a decline of 4.49 percentage points.
problem_reframe.complication: Deterioration spans Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, Conventional Engine Oil and Compressor Oil, while periods 2026-006 through 2026-008 show positive movements and are marked within threshold. No named healthy product benchmark is supplied. Anchor-account list prices are locked mid-quarter, and the proposed explanations of input inflation, superior premium economics and structural decline remain hypotheses rather than established causes.
problem_reframe.question: Which contract-compliant intervention should be authorized to recover affected-product margins without transferring volume into unverified alternatives or confusing segment recovery with enterprise improvement?

key_assumptions.assumption: The 20.64% current margin and 7.14-point deterioration describe Synthetic Blend Engine Oil.
key_assumptions.provenance: The Synthetic Blend Engine Oil change point explicitly reports 20.64% current, 27.78% previous and a negative 7.14-point delta.

key_assumptions.assumption: At least part of the affected products' deterioration is operationally or commercially recoverable.
key_assumptions.provenance: Executed supplier terms, customer renewals or assortment changes subsequently increase realized product gross profit after implementation costs.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Renewal pricing and supplier savings can claim overlapping recovery from the same 7.14-point Synthetic Blend deterioration.
unresolved_tensions.requires: CFO assigns non-overlapping benefit ownership and a combined margin bridge before either intervention's first benefit claim, by Week 2.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Forward purchasing can preserve supply economics but obstruct subsequent assortment withdrawal.
unresolved_tensions.requires: Chief Procurement Officer caps forward commitments at retained committed demand before signing supplier agreements, by Week 2.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Margin-percentage recovery may conflict with retaining account contribution and enterprise gross-profit dollars.
unresolved_tensions.requires: Chief Commercial Officer approves account-level retention and contribution floors before issuing renewal or withdrawal notices, by Week 2.

blind_spots: No separate SITUATION METRICS block is supplied; KPI name and unit are taken from the analysis, and the headline-versus-segment inconsistency is explicitly separated.
The supplied breakdowns identify where margin deteriorated, not whether input inflation, discounting or structural demand changes caused it.

proposed_option.title: Cost-Component Waterfall & Reallocation Decision: Isolate Base Oil vs. Distribution vs. Manufacturing Inflation
proposed_option.description: Conduct a 30-day cost-component decomposition of COGS for Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil to isolate whether margin loss is driven by base oil price escalation, freight/distribution inflation, or manufacturing/packaging cost creep. Use findings to decide between: (a) accepting lower margin in Value/Conventional tier and reallocating portfolio emphasis to higher-resilience SKUs, or (b) negotiating supplier contracts for base oil and freight, or (c) exiting or de-emphasizing the most-pressured SKU within the next quarter.
proposed_option.mechanism: The hypothesis rests on COGS movement (confirmed direct relationship), not revenue decline. Decomposing COGS into base_oil_cost, distribution_cost, manufacturing_cost, and packaging_cost (all confirmed INDIRECT drivers via COGS) will identify which cost account is inflating. This isolates whether the margin loss is: (1) structural/durable (commodity input inflation → portfolio reallocation needed), (2) tactical/contractual (freight spike → negotiable), or (3) operational (manufacturing inefficiency → process fix). The constraint against mid-quarter price increases means revenue-side recovery is unavailable; cost isolation is the only frame-respecting lever.

impact_estimate.basis: Partial recovery assumes cost isolation identifies 35–50% of the 7.14-point compression as addressable via supplier negotiation or SKU reallocation (e.g., shifting volume mix toward higher-resilience products or renegotiating base oil contracts). Full recovery (7.14 points) is unlikely within 90 days given commodity dynamics and contractual constraints; realistic recovery targets 2.5–4.5 points through tactical cost management and portfolio shift.
